transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... well, I guess I'm just having some trouble slowing down. It feels like I'm constantly running on a motor lately. I'll finish one thing at school, or at home, and... I just immediately jump into the next thing. I just can't seem to shut myself off. That's mainly it.
Has this feeling of constantly running on a motor been happening for most of your life, or is this something that started more recently?
Um... more recently, I suppose. It hasn't always been this intense. Just for the last eight months or so. That's... well, that's when an older relative moved in with us.
Besides feeling like you're running on a motor, how has your mood been overall during these past eight months? Would you say you've been feeling unusually happy, energetic, or elevated?

Um... no. Not really. I wouldn't say I'm unusually happy. Just... normal, I suppose. My mood is fine. I just... I just have all this energy that I can't turn off. But no, not... elevated or anything like that.
Before this relative moved in eight months ago, did you have any trouble with restlessness, difficulty focusing, or needing to stay busy—even if it wasn't as intense as now?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. It's not just from the last eight months. 

My mother... well, she used to joke about it when I was a kid. Back in elementary school. She'd say I was trying to teach the class from my seat. I was just... always getting out of my chair. Talking, or cutting in before the teacher even finished giving directions. 

So... yes. It's been a part of who I am for a long time. Long before I was an adult. It isn't just something that started with this family change.

Around the time your relative moved in eight months ago, did anything else happen—like you being sick with a high fever or infection, hitting your head, starting any new medications, or any other medical issues?
Um... no. Nothing like that. I haven't been sick. No new medications or... head injuries. Just the same as always, medically speaking.
When you're trying to focus on homework or read something, do you find it hard to concentrate, or do you find your mind wandering to other things?
Um... no. Not really. I can focus fine when I need to read something. I haven't really noticed my mind wandering.

When you're doing something that doesn't interest you much—like chores or a boring task—do you find yourself getting restless and wanting to move on to something else, or do you find yourself worrying about things and feeling tense?
Um... no, not really. I don't get worried or tense about chores. I just... do them. I don't think I get restless either. It's just normal stuff.

When you say you can't turn off your energy and you're running on a motor—what does that actually look like? Are you fidgeting a lot, moving around, having trouble sitting still? Or is it more that you're talking a lot?

I guess... it's just hard to sit still. Like, when I'm in IEP meetings or taking admin classes, I'm always moving. My leg bounces under the table, or I'm clicking a pen. I shift around in my chair a lot. Sometimes I don't even realize I'm doing it until I see people looking at me.
Do you find yourself doing things without thinking first—like interrupting people, blurting things out, or making quick decisions you later regret?

I suppose... I do jump in sometimes. Like if my colleagues are talking, or parents... even my wife and her sister. I just... I think I'm helping. But I guess I end up talking over them. Or I just take over before they're done speaking.
When you're working on a task at school or at home, do you often make careless mistakes, or do you find it hard to pay attention to details even when you're trying to concentrate?
I don't think so. I mean... my work gets done. I haven't really noticed making careless mistakes or anything like that.

You mentioned you can focus fine when reading something and haven't noticed your mind wandering. But I want to ask more specifically: when you're working on something that requires sustained attention—like grading papers or filling out forms—do you find yourself getting easily distracted by other things going on around you, or do you lose track of time and forget what you were supposed to be doing?

No... I don't really have an issue with that. I mean, if I have to grade or fill out the IEP forms... I just do it. I haven't really noticed getting pulled away by other things or forgetting what I'm doing.

You mentioned you can focus when reading and don't lose track during tasks like grading. But I'm curious—when you're in meetings or doing administrative work, do you ever struggle to listen to what others are saying? Like, do you find yourself thinking about what you want to say next instead of really hearing what someone is telling you?
Not really, no. I mean... I hear what people are saying. I'm listening to them. I don't think I have a problem with that.
